required_manual_checks.description: The contract makes the already-promoted 2A.3b (Priority) and 2A.3c (one pipeline, stage summary) live and nothing else: build and serve one pinned PROMOTED baseline SHA. No migration, no schema, grant or data change, no new behavior, and no unrelated production change. It states the undeployed range (the serving pin ad86aa2 to the deploy pin) and lists every changed path in that range from git, classifying each as code, test, doc or tooling, so a reviewer can see nothing else ships.

Prove, with evidence, that the deploy needs no database change: core/db/schema and the migration ledger are byte-identical between ad86aa2 and the deploy pin; the 2A.3b/2A.3c reads use only objects 001-010 created, under the existing grants and RLS (cite the SQL); the new build needs no environment name production lacks; and the CURRENT recovery point (post-010, profile post-010-v1) remains valid for the deploy tree (the profile registry and recovery-points.ts are unchanged, or the difference is explained). State whether a pre-deploy backup is required; the recommendation must be justified by the fact that the deploy writes nothing, and the choice goes to the owner as a decision.

Because the schema does not change, the old build IS a valid rollback, unlike 2A.3a. Specify it exactly: a copy-on-write clone of the serving .next and the old pin recorded before the stop; the rollback trigger (any smoke FAIL after the restart); and the rollback steps (stop, restore the clone at the old pin, start, re-run the baseline smoke). The serving checkout switch (detached ad86aa2 to the detached deploy pin) is part of the window and is reversed by the rollback. Respect the recorded build/restart race: the service is restarted AFTER the build completes, never raced against it.

deploy-smoke.mjs gains the 2A.3b/2A.3c checks while staying write-free. (1) The expected-to-fail-on-the-old-build marker is scoped to a named release, selected explicitly (e.g. --release 2a3bc), so the 2A.3a checks (C1-C7, R2-R4), which now pass on the old build, are ordinary checks for this rollout and the new checks carry the discrimination; the 2A.3a behavior stays reproducible for the historical record. (2) New checks, owner AND partner: /sales shows the Priority section first and its section-nav entry; /sales/list?priority=1 loads titled Priority; /sales shows the open-pipeline-by-stage summary whose links carry the viewer's scope; /partner answers a redirect to /sales and ?scope=team is forwarded; no authenticated page offers a link to /partner. (3) A6 no longer expects /partner to load 200: it asserts the redirect instead, with the same witnessed-specification comment convention A10 uses. (4) Every new check is marked for the release so the baseline run on the old build proves discrimination, and the baseline must show zero UNEXPECTED-PASS. The existing guarantees hold: only login writes, every other POST/PATCH/DELETE targets the ghost reference, partner credentials only from the environment and never printed.

tests/architecture/rollout-2a3bc.test.ts (classified in gate-2g1.ts in the same change) holds the smoke to the release model by source text: every 2A.3bc check id is marked for that release; the release selector is required in --baseline and --post; A6 asserts the /partner redirect; the write-free guarantees still hold. rollout-010.test.ts is updated only as far as the release scoping requires, and its 2A.3a assertions keep their meaning (every 2A.3a check still marked for release 2a3a). Mutants: removing a release marker, letting a new check pass on the old build unmarked, and restoring A6's 200 expectation each turn a test red.

The contract lists preconditions (P-rows) and the sequence (T-rows) with a pass condition and a failure row for every step, modeled on SLICE-2A3A-EXECUTION-CONTRACT.md: Coordinator verify after fetching agents/coord and review/*; full aggregate green on the exact deploy tree including owner R1b/R1c via prove --owner; serving tree clean with no iCloud duplicates in source or .next; only the launchd com.ascend.os process on 3001; baseline smoke on the old build with the partner's credentials (discrimination: every release check fails as expected, no UNEXPECTED-PASS); the rollback clone; stop; switch the serving checkout to the pin; build; verify no iCloud duplicates; start; post smoke (every check passes, owner and partner, nothing written); owner acceptance by looking at /sales as himself. Every production-touching or credential-bearing command is run by Oscar in his own terminal.

Section for decisions recorded at authorization: the deploy SHA and tree (the latest PROMOTED baseline at authorization, pinned exactly), the window, the rollback policy (the old build is valid; roll back on any post-smoke FAIL), whether to take a pre-deploy backup, and serving-tree hygiene. Carry forward the open follow-ups that touch this window (I1 iCloud serving tree; R1c intermittency) as recorded risks, not new work.

The builder does not contact production, read .env.production.local values, or run the smoke against the live service. The smoke is exercised only against the fixture-PG17 dev server (never production) in both release modes, and that run is recorded in the contract's evidence section.

title: Rollout contract and smoke for 2A.3b + 2A.3c: a code-only deploy of the promoted baseline (no migration, no production contact)
